title: Edge Model Service Runbook
summary: Qualify and operate an edge model under device, power, connectivity, physical-access, privacy, update, and recovery constraints.
prerequisites: A device, location, connectivity, power, and physical-access inventory
An optimized model and runtime candidate with license and provenance evidence
An update, fleet-observability, safe-degradation, and device-recovery owner

sections.title: Design for the real device and environment
paragraphs: Record processor and accelerator, execution provider, memory, storage, thermal envelope, power source, operating system, secure boot or device-trust capabilities, sensors, local users, physical access, connectivity windows, clock behavior, and replacement process. Select a model and conversion that fit the device under sustained representative work, not only a short laboratory request.

Define which data stays on device, what telemetry may leave, how identity and policy work while disconnected, what features degrade safely, and which operations must stop. Local inference can reduce data movement, but it does not automatically protect exposed devices, local caches, removable storage, logs, model intellectual property, or downstream tool effects.

sections.title: Qualify offline behavior and fleet lifecycle
paragraphs: Pin the original model revision and digest, conversion or quantization recipe, converted artifact digest, runtime and execution-provider versions, device policy, and application adapter. Evaluate the converted build itself for important slices, safety boundaries, numerical or quality drift, latency, energy, sustained heat, memory pressure, storage growth, reboot, clock error, damaged input, disconnected operation, and dependency failure.

Stage signed or otherwise integrity-verified updates to a small authorized cohort, preserve a compatible fallback, bound download and storage use, verify after reboot, and report fleet state without collecting unnecessary content. A device that misses updates beyond policy, loses trustworthy identity, cannot report critical state, or fails rollback must move to a defined limited or offline mode.

Offline contract: [IDENTITY, POLICY, CACHE, CLOCK, TELEMETRY BUFFER, EXPIRY, AND PROHIBITED ACTIONS]
Fleet limits: [MEMORY, STORAGE, THERMAL, ENERGY, REQUEST, RETRY, UPDATE COHORT, AND STALENESS]
Verification: [CONVERTED-BUILD EVAL, SUSTAINED LOAD, POWER/NETWORK LOSS, REBOOT, UPDATE, ROLLBACK, AND FLEET STATE]
Stop conditions: [UNTRUSTED ARTIFACT/DEVICE, CRITICAL QUALITY DRIFT, DATA LEAK, THERMAL/POWER LIMIT, EXPIRED POLICY, OR FAILED ROLLBACK]
Recovery: [ENTER SAFE MODE, ISOLATE DEVICE/COHORT, RECONCILE BUFFERED WORK, RESTORE PINNED BUILD, REENROLL OR REPLACE]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the device and environment profile, source and converted artifact identities, license and provenance decision, conversion recipe, runtime compatibility, converted-build evaluation, sustained performance and power observations, offline and clock behavior, data and telemetry policy, update cohort evidence, rollback or replacement rehearsal, fleet owner, and review date.

Verify at least one loss-of-connectivity or power transition and one failed update. Stop or limit operation on identity loss, artifact mismatch, critical quality drift, prohibited data movement, unsafe temperature or power behavior, expired policy, or failed rollback. Isolate the device or cohort, preserve minimal evidence, reconcile buffered and external effects, restore the pinned build or reenroll a clean device, and verify the safe state before return.

sections.title: Completed fictional qualification record and deployment HOLD
paragraphs: This completed record preserves the original operational scope. Its concrete values describe a fictional classroom design, not observed hardware. Declared device class: EDGE-CLASSROOM-ARM64-01. Declared processor: fictional four-core ARM64 processor. Declared accelerator: none. Declared memory: 4 GiB. Declared persistent storage: 32 GiB. Declared operating system: FictionOS 1.0. Declared secure boot: enabled. Declared sensors: one temperature channel and one input-power channel. Declared power source: 12 V DC adapter with battery-backed orderly shutdown. Declared connectivity: Ethernet primary, Wi-Fi secondary, and disconnected operation permitted only under a valid local lease. Declared physical placement: locked indoor cabinet with operator-controlled service access. Declared clock behavior: wall clock is untrusted; same-process lease duration uses monotonic elapsed time; process or device restart invalidates the lease. Declared replacement process: isolate, preserve minimal evidence, install a newly enrolled device, restore a pinned compatible artifact, and reauthorize it. None of these fictional hardware declarations has inspection, bill-of-materials, secure-boot attestation, calibration, or deployment evidence.

Task: classify fictional local sensor records without external side effects. Safe degradation: deny inference and updates when identity, policy, artifact integrity, checkpoint structure, connectivity rules, or fixture readings are uncertain. The classroom program never sends telemetry, invokes a model runtime, operates a sensor, or performs an external effect. It therefore cannot replay an uncertain external effect. Scope: one fictional device, one fictional indoor location, an enrolled operator, fixture temperature and power inputs, no prompts or model outputs in telemetry, bounded local persistence, intermittent connectivity, and controlled physical access. Permissions: local fixture reauthorization only, integrity verification of pinned classroom bytes, no real credential, no private data, no remote action, and no production update authority.

Exact classroom build: baseline bytes are `fictional-baseline-model-v1` with SHA-256 `932d8e5a203d4c867e770d74ecb7c5e3e6d2d652a168143123b1579cb56534b2`; candidate bytes are `fictional-converted-model-v2` with SHA-256 `d7db9091598c61c4e09f96c4c9552b904f5d08bbffe7402ffc6510d77e468d66`. These are fictional byte fixtures, not models. The source-model revision, source-model digest, conversion recipe, converted ONNX graph, license decision, inference runtime, execution-provider version, application adapter, and real model-card evidence are UNKNOWN because they were not supplied. The classroom state machine trusts immutable expected digests in its source, persists the bytes, and verifies the active bytes at startup rather than accepting a caller-supplied digest.

Offline contract: identity loss immediately persists containment. Link loss changes connectivity state but does not extend authorization. Reconnection alone does not restore identity or policy. The local policy lease lasts 30 monotonic seconds within one process session. A backward wall-clock change cannot extend it. A reconstructed process invalidates the persisted lease and denies work until the explicit authenticated fixture reauthorization method is called. This is intentionally stricter than treating a newly created monotonic clock as continuation across a reboot. Only typed values for `device_id`, `state`, `event`, and `elapsed_seconds` may enter the telemetry queue. The queue capacity is three. Prompts, outputs, sensor payloads, credentials, arbitrary event text, and secret-bearing values are rejected.

Declared fixture limits are 0.0 through 85.0 degrees Celsius and 0.0 through 25.0 watts, inclusive. Boolean values, strings, nonfinite numbers, negative numbers, and values above either declared maximum are unsafe. These thresholds exercise control flow only. They are never represented as measured limits, calibrated sensor results, or evidence that a physical device can operate safely.

Fleet lifecycle: stage integrity-verified updates to an authorized cohort; preserve a verified compatible baseline; bound storage and telemetry; verify persisted active bytes after restart; and retain containment after artifact, checkpoint, identity, policy, reading, or recovery failure. Stop conditions are untrusted identity, expired policy, malformed state, artifact mismatch, critical quality drift, prohibited data movement, unsafe thermal or power evidence, or failed rollback. Recovery enters safe mode, isolates the device or cohort, preserves minimal evidence, reconciles only confirmed buffered work, restores a verified compatible pinned build when one exists, and requires reauthorization before return.

Qualification status: HOLD. Processor, accelerator, memory, storage, secure boot, sensors, physical-access control, power behavior, connectivity behavior, clock behavior across an actual reboot, replacement rehearsal, model conversion, license, runtime compatibility, inference quality, sustained latency, memory pressure, energy, temperature, throttling, update cohort, rollback, and fleet reporting are all unobserved. Classroom publication, passing tests, a model card, or a successful conversion must not be used as deployment acceptance.

Authoritative references checked 2026-09-20: ONNX Runtime edge deployment guidance, https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/tutorials/iot-edge/; ONNX Runtime execution providers, https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/execution-providers/; Hugging Face model-card documentation, https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards; NIST AI Risk Management Framework, https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework; Python monotonic-clock documentation, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/time.html#time.monotonic; Python `os.replace` documentation, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/os.html#os.replace; Python JSON documentation, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/json.html; and Python hashing documentation, https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/hashlib.html.

sections.title: Runnable Python 3.11+ classroom state machine
paragraphs: Prerequisites: Python 3.11 or newer; permission to create `edge_learning_runs` beneath the current working directory; and enough local storage for small JSON and fictional artifact files. There are no external dependencies, network calls, credentials, private data, temporary-directory calls, or destructive cleanup operations. Every invocation creates a unique UUID-named subfolder inside the learner-owned `edge_learning_runs` folder. Old runs are not deleted or reused, while printed output remains stable.

Save the following complete file as `edge_operations.py`. The manifest is the sole authoritative state record. Each manifest update writes a sibling file, flushes it with `fsync`, and atomically replaces the prior manifest with `os.replace`. Artifact files are persisted separately, but an artifact becomes staged or active only through an atomic manifest commit. Extra candidate bytes left by a crash before a manifest commit are not authoritative. Startup validates the exact manifest schema, typed and bounded telemetry values, pinned artifact names and digests, active and staged artifact bytes, and policy-session status. A malformed manifest or corrupt active artifact produces persisted containment rather than a fabricated healthy fallback.

The test runner aggregates every failure. It prints `ALL NEGATIVE TESTS PASS` only when all six top-level tests pass, and it returns a nonzero process status if any test fails. The first top-level group launches the same reviewed file through `sys.executable` with a private `--probe-root` CLI mode, then verifies that a separately started Python process denies the prior process lease. The probe uses the learner-owned run folder and no external package, temporary-directory service, or deletion. Repeated `--tests` invocations use new run folders, so a previous full telemetry queue cannot contaminate a later result.

code.label: edge_operations.py
code.code:
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

RUNS_ROOT = Path("edge_learning_runs")
BASELINE_BYTES = b"fictional-baseline-model-v1"
CANDIDATE_BYTES = b"fictional-converted-model-v2"
BASELINE_DIGEST = "932d8e5a203d4c867e770d74ecb7c5e3e6d2d652a168143123b1579cb56534b2"
CANDIDATE_DIGEST = "d7db9091598c61c4e09f96c4c9552b904f5d08bbffe7402ffc6510d77e468d66"
EXPECTED = {
    "baseline": ("baseline.bin", BASELINE_DIGEST),
    "candidate": ("candidate.bin", CANDIDATE_DIGEST),
}
AUTH_FIXTURE = "CLASSROOM-AUTH-FIXTURE"
QUEUE_LIMIT = 3
LEASE_SECONDS = 30.0
MIN_TEMP_C = 0.0
MAX_TEMP_C = 85.0
MIN_WATTS = 0.0
MAX_WATTS = 25.0
ALLOWED_STATES = {"ready", "offline", "contained"}
ALLOWED_EVENTS = {"boot", "link-loss", "reconnect", "update-staged"}
MANIFEST_KEYS = {
    "version", "active", "staged", "safe", "reason", "identity",
    "connected", "policy", "queue", "uncertain_external_effects"
}
POLICY_KEYS = {"authorized", "session", "lease_seconds"}
TELEMETRY_KEYS = {"device_id", "state", "event", "elapsed_seconds"}
PRESERVED_CONTAINMENT_REASONS = {
    "failed-recovery", "malformed-fallback-compatibility"
}


class Denied(Exception):
    pass


class InjectedPowerLoss(RuntimeError):
    pass


def sha256(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def new_run_folder():
    RUNS_ROOT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    while True:
        folder = RUNS_ROOT / str(uuid.uuid4())
        try:
            folder.mkdir()
            return folder
        except FileExistsError:
            continue


def is_plain_number(value):
    return type(value) in (int, float) and math.isfinite(value)


class Machine:
    def __init__(self, root, wall_clock=None, monotonic=None):
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.wall_clock = wall_clock if wall_clock is not None else time.time
        self.monotonic = monotonic if monotonic is not None else time.monotonic
        self.session = uuid.uuid4().hex
        self.deadline = None
        self.manifest_path = self.root / "manifest.json"
        if not self.manifest_path.exists():
            self._initialize()
        self.state = self._load_or_contain()
        self._invalidate_lease_after_restart()

    def _default_manifest(self, safe=True, reason="authorization-required"):
        return {
            "version": 1,
            "active": "baseline",
            "staged": None,
            "safe": safe,
            "reason": reason,
            "identity": "trusted",
            "connected": True,
            "policy": {
                "authorized": False,
                "session": None,
                "lease_seconds": LEASE_SECONDS,
            },
            "queue": [],
            "uncertain_external_effects": [],
        }

    def _initialize(self):
        self._write_artifact("baseline", BASELINE_BYTES)
        self.state = self._default_manifest()
        self._save()

    def _write_bytes_atomic(self, path, data):
        sibling = path.with_name(path.name + ".new")
        with sibling.open("wb") as handle:
            handle.write(data)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(sibling, path)

    def _write_artifact(self, name, data):
        filename, expected_digest = EXPECTED[name]
        if sha256(data) != expected_digest:
            raise Denied("artifact digest mismatch")
        self._write_bytes_atomic(self.root / filename, data)

    def _save(self):
        encoded = json.dumps(
            self.state, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
        ).encode("utf-8")
        self._write_bytes_atomic(self.manifest_path, encoded)

    def _validate_telemetry(self, event):
        if type(event) is not dict or set(event) != TELEMETRY_KEYS:
            raise ValueError("telemetry schema")
        if type(event["device_id"]) is not str or event["device_id"] != "CLASSROOM-1":
            raise ValueError("telemetry device_id")
        if type(event["state"]) is not str or event["state"] not in ALLOWED_STATES:
            raise ValueError("telemetry state")
        if type(event["event"]) is not str or event["event"] not in ALLOWED_EVENTS:
            raise ValueError("telemetry event")
        elapsed = event["elapsed_seconds"]
        if type(elapsed) is not int or not 0 <= elapsed <= 86400:
            raise ValueError("telemetry elapsed_seconds")

    def _validate_manifest(self, value):
        if type(value) is not dict or set(value) != MANIFEST_KEYS:
            raise ValueError("manifest schema")
        if type(value["version"]) is not int or value["version"] != 1:
            raise ValueError("manifest version")
        if type(value["active"]) is not str or value["active"] not in EXPECTED:
            raise ValueError("active slot")
        if value["staged"] is not None and (
            type(value["staged"]) is not str or value["staged"] != "candidate"
        ):
            raise ValueError("staged slot")
        if type(value["safe"]) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("safe type")
        if value["reason"] is not None and type(value["reason"]) is not str:
            raise ValueError("reason type")
        if type(value["reason"]) is str and len(value["reason"]) > 80:
            raise ValueError("reason length")
        if value["identity"] not in ("trusted", "lost"):
            raise ValueError("identity")
        if type(value["connected"]) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("connected type")
        policy = value["policy"]
        if type(policy) is not dict or set(policy) != POLICY_KEYS:
            raise ValueError("policy schema")
        if type(policy["authorized"]) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("policy authorized")
        if policy["session"] is not None and type(policy["session"]) is not str:
            raise ValueError("policy session")
        if type(policy["session"]) is str and len(policy["session"]) != 32:
            raise ValueError("policy session length")
        if type(policy["lease_seconds"]) is not float:
            raise ValueError("policy lease type")
        if policy["lease_seconds"] != LEASE_SECONDS:
            raise ValueError("policy lease value")
        queue = value["queue"]
        if type(queue) is not list or len(queue) > QUEUE_LIMIT:
            raise ValueError("queue bound")
        for event in queue:
            self._validate_telemetry(event)
        effects = value["uncertain_external_effects"]
        if type(effects) is not list or effects:
            raise ValueError("uncertain external effects")

    def _artifact_valid(self, name):
        filename, expected_digest = EXPECTED[name]
        path = self.root / filename
        try:
            return path.is_file() and sha256(path.read_bytes()) == expected_digest
        except OSError:
            return False

    def _persist_containment(self, reason, preserve_active=True):
        if preserve_active and hasattr(self, "state") and self.state.get("active") in EXPECTED:
            active = self.state["active"]
        else:
            active = "baseline"
        self.state = self._default_manifest(safe=True, reason=reason)
        self.state["active"] = active
        self._save()
        return self.state

    def _load_or_contain(self):
        try:
            value = json.loads(self.manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self._validate_manifest(value)
            self.state = value
        except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError):
            return self._persist_containment("manifest-corrupt", preserve_active=False)
        if not self._artifact_valid(self.state["active"]):
            reason = "active-artifact-corrupt"
            if (
                self.state["safe"]
                and self.state["reason"] in PRESERVED_CONTAINMENT_REASONS
            ):
                reason = self.state["reason"]
            return self._persist_containment(reason)
        if self.state["staged"] is not None and not self._artifact_valid("candidate"):
            return self._persist_containment("staged-artifact-corrupt")
        return self.state

    def _invalidate_lease_after_restart(self):
        policy = self.state["policy"]
        if policy["authorized"] or policy["session"] is not None:
            policy["authorized"] = False
            policy["session"] = None
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "restart-reauthorization-required"
            self.deadline = None
            self._save()

    def reauthorize(self, fixture_token):
        if fixture_token != AUTH_FIXTURE:
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "authentication-failed"
            self._save()
            raise Denied("authentication failed")
        if self.state["identity"] != "trusted":
            raise Denied("identity untrusted")
        if not self._artifact_valid(self.state["active"]):
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "active-artifact-corrupt"
            self._save()
            raise Denied("active artifact corrupt")
        self.deadline = self.monotonic() + LEASE_SECONDS
        self.state["policy"] = {
            "authorized": True,
            "session": self.session,
            "lease_seconds": LEASE_SECONDS,
        }
        self.state["safe"] = False
        self.state["reason"] = None
        self._save()

    def policy_valid(self):
        policy = self.state["policy"]
        return (
            policy["authorized"]
            and policy["session"] == self.session
            and self.deadline is not None
            and self.monotonic() < self.deadline
        )

    def authorize(self):
        if self.state["safe"]:
            raise Denied("safe mode")
        if self.state["identity"] != "trusted":
            raise Denied("identity untrusted")
        if not self.policy_valid():
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "policy-expired-or-untrusted"
            self.state["policy"]["authorized"] = False
            self.state["policy"]["session"] = None
            self.deadline = None
            self._save()
            raise Denied("policy expired or untrusted")
        if not self._artifact_valid(self.state["active"]):
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "active-artifact-corrupt"
            self._save()
            raise Denied("active artifact corrupt")

    def telemetry(self, **fields):
        try:
            self._validate_telemetry(fields)
        except ValueError as error:
            raise Denied("privacy allowlist") from error
        if len(self.state["queue"]) >= QUEUE_LIMIT:
            raise Denied("telemetry queue full")
        self.state["queue"].append(dict(fields))
        self._save()

    def link_lost(self):
        self.state["connected"] = False
        self._save()

    def reconnect(self, fixture_token):
        self.state["connected"] = True
        self._save()
        self.reauthorize(fixture_token)

    def lose_identity(self):
        self.state["identity"] = "lost"
        self.state["safe"] = True
        self.state["reason"] = "identity-lost"
        self.state["policy"]["authorized"] = False
        self.state["policy"]["session"] = None
        self.deadline = None
        self._save()

    def reenroll_identity(self, fixture_token):
        if fixture_token != AUTH_FIXTURE:
            raise Denied("authentication failed")
        self.state["identity"] = "trusted"
        self._save()
        self.reauthorize(fixture_token)

    def reading(self, temperature_c, watts):
        valid = (
            is_plain_number(temperature_c)
            and is_plain_number(watts)
            and MIN_TEMP_C <= temperature_c <= MAX_TEMP_C
            and MIN_WATTS <= watts <= MAX_WATTS
        )
        if not valid:
            self.state["safe"] = True
            self.state["reason"] = "unsafe-fixture-reading"
            self._save()
            raise Denied("unsafe fixture reading")

    def _crash(self, selected, point):
        if selected == point:
            raise InjectedPowerLoss(point)

    def update(self, fail_at=None):
        self.authorize()
        self._crash(fail_at, "before-candidate-write")
        self._write_artifact("candidate", CANDIDATE_BYTES)
        self._crash(fail_at, "after-candidate-write")
        self._crash(fail_at, "before-stage-commit")
        self.state["staged"] = "candidate"
        self._save()
        self._crash(fail_at, "after-stage-commit")
        if not self._artifact_valid("candidate"):
            raise Denied("candidate artifact corrupt")
        self._crash(fail_at, "after-verify")
        if self.state["active"] != "baseline" or not self._artifact_valid("baseline"):
            raise Denied("no compatible baseline transition")
        self._crash(fail_at, "before-activate-commit")
        self.state["active"] = "candidate"
        self.state["staged"] = None
        self._save()
        self._crash(fail_at, "after-activate-commit")

    def recover(self, fallback_compatible=True):
        if type(fallback_compatible) is not bool:
            self._persist_containment("malformed-fallback-compatibility")
            raise Denied("malformed fallback compatibility flag")
        if self._artifact_valid(self.state["active"]):
            self.state["staged"] = None
            self._save()
            return
        if not fallback_compatible or not self._artifact_valid("baseline"):
            self._persist_containment("failed-recovery")
            raise Denied("no compatible fallback")
        self.state["active"] = "baseline"
        self.state["staged"] = None
        self.state["safe"] = True
        self.state["reason"] = "restored-awaiting-reauthorization"
        self.state["policy"]["authorized"] = False
        self.state["policy"]["session"] = None
        self.deadline = None
        self._save()


def expect_denied(action, message=None):
    try:
        action()
    except Denied as error:
        if message is not None and str(error) != message:
            raise AssertionError("wrong denial: " + str(error)) from error
        return
    raise AssertionError("operation was not denied")


def test_expiry_and_restart(root):
    clock = {"mono": 0.0, "wall": 1_700_000_000.0}
    mono = lambda: clock["mono"]
    wall = lambda: clock["wall"]
    machine = Machine(root / "expiry", wall, mono)
    machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    clock["mono"] = 31.0
    clock["wall"] -= 100_000.0
    expect_denied(machine.authorize, "policy expired or untrusted")
    second = Machine(root / "restart", wall, mono)
    second.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    restarted = Machine(root / "restart", wall, mono)
    expect_denied(restarted.authorize, "safe mode")

    process_folder = root / "process-restart"
    process_machine = Machine(process_folder)
    process_machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    completed = subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(Path(__file__).resolve()),
            "--probe-root",
            str(process_folder.resolve()),
        ],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
        check=False,
    )
    assert completed.returncode == 0, completed.stderr
    assert completed.stderr == ""
    assert completed.stdout == (
        "PROBE restart_policy=DENIED "
        "reason=restart-reauthorization-required\n"
    )


def test_queue_privacy_connectivity_identity(root):
    machine = Machine(root / "queue")
    machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    for number in range(3):
        machine.telemetry(
            device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state="ready",
            event="boot", elapsed_seconds=number
        )
    expect_denied(
        lambda: machine.telemetry(
            device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state="ready",
            event="boot", elapsed_seconds=3
        ),
        "telemetry queue full",
    )
    expect_denied(
        lambda: machine.telemetry(
            device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state="ready",
            event="secret payload", elapsed_seconds=3
        ),
        "privacy allowlist",
    )
    expect_denied(
        lambda: machine.telemetry(
            device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state=[],
            event="boot", elapsed_seconds=3
        ),
        "privacy allowlist",
    )
    expect_denied(
        lambda: machine.telemetry(
            device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state="ready",
            event=[], elapsed_seconds=3
        ),
        "privacy allowlist",
    )
    machine.link_lost()
    assert machine.state["connected"] is False
    machine.reconnect(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    machine.lose_identity()
    expect_denied(machine.authorize, "safe mode")
    machine.reenroll_identity(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    assert machine.state["connected"] is True


def test_power_boundaries(root):
    points = (
        "before-candidate-write", "after-candidate-write",
        "before-stage-commit", "after-stage-commit", "after-verify",
        "before-activate-commit", "after-activate-commit",
    )
    for point in points:
        folder = root / ("power-" + point)
        machine = Machine(folder)
        machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
        try:
            machine.update(fail_at=point)
        except InjectedPowerLoss:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("power loss not injected at " + point)
        restarted = Machine(folder)
        restarted.recover()
        expected_active = "candidate" if point == "after-activate-commit" else "baseline"
        assert restarted.state["active"] == expected_active
        assert restarted._artifact_valid(restarted.state["active"])


def test_corrupt_manifest_and_artifact(root):
    malformed = Machine(root / "malformed")
    malformed.manifest_path.write_text(
        json.dumps({"safe": "false", "queue": ["secret"]}),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    contained = Machine(root / "malformed")
    assert contained.state["safe"] is True
    assert contained.state["reason"] == "manifest-corrupt"
    expect_denied(contained.authorize, "safe mode")

    malformed_active = Machine(root / "malformed-active")
    malformed_active_value = malformed_active._default_manifest()
    malformed_active_value["active"] = []
    malformed_active.manifest_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(malformed_active_value), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    malformed_active_restarted = Machine(root / "malformed-active")
    assert malformed_active_restarted.state["safe"] is True
    assert malformed_active_restarted.state["reason"] == "manifest-corrupt"
    expect_denied(malformed_active_restarted.authorize, "safe mode")

    corrupt = Machine(root / "artifact")
    corrupt.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    (corrupt.root / "baseline.bin").write_bytes(b"corrupt")
    restarted = Machine(root / "artifact")
    assert restarted.state["safe"] is True
    assert restarted.state["reason"] == "active-artifact-corrupt"
    expect_denied(restarted.authorize, "safe mode")


def test_incompatible_fallback_and_failed_recovery(root):
    folder = root / "fallback"
    machine = Machine(folder)
    machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    machine.update()
    (folder / "candidate.bin").write_bytes(b"corrupt")
    restarted = Machine(folder)
    expect_denied(lambda: restarted.recover(False), "no compatible fallback")
    final = Machine(folder)
    assert final.state["safe"] is True
    assert final.state["reason"] == "failed-recovery"
    assert final.state["active"] == "candidate"
    expect_denied(final.authorize, "safe mode")

    malformed_folder = root / "malformed-fallback-flag"
    malformed = Machine(malformed_folder)
    malformed.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    malformed.update()
    (malformed_folder / "candidate.bin").write_bytes(b"corrupt")
    malformed_restarted = Machine(malformed_folder)
    expect_denied(
        lambda: malformed_restarted.recover("false"),
        "malformed fallback compatibility flag",
    )
    malformed_final = Machine(malformed_folder)
    assert malformed_final.state["safe"] is True
    assert malformed_final.state["reason"] == "malformed-fallback-compatibility"
    assert malformed_final.state["active"] == "candidate"
    assert malformed_final._artifact_valid("baseline")
    assert not malformed_final._artifact_valid("candidate")
    expect_denied(malformed_final.authorize, "safe mode")


def test_reading_bounds(root):
    bad_values = (
        (float("nan"), 1.0), (1.0, float("inf")),
        (-0.1, 1.0), (1.0, -0.1),
        (85.1, 1.0), (1.0, 25.1),
        (True, 1.0), (1.0, False),
        ("20", 1.0), (20.0, "5"),
    )
    for index, values in enumerate(bad_values):
        machine = Machine(root / ("reading-" + str(index)))
        machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
        expect_denied(lambda m=machine, v=values: m.reading(*v), "unsafe fixture reading")
        assert machine.state["safe"] is True


def run_tests():
    root = new_run_folder()
    cases = (
        ("expiry, backward wall clock, and restart denial", test_expiry_and_restart),
        ("queue saturation, privacy, connectivity, and identity", test_queue_privacy_connectivity_identity),
        ("power loss at every persisted update boundary", test_power_boundaries),
        ("corrupted checkpoint and persisted artifact", test_corrupt_manifest_and_artifact),
        ("incompatible fallback and failed recovery", test_incompatible_fallback_and_failed_recovery),
        ("nonfinite, negative, boolean, malformed, and over-limit readings", test_reading_bounds),
    )
    failures = []
    for name, function in cases:
        try:
            function(root)
        except Exception as error:
            failures.append((name, error))
            print("FAIL " + name + ": " + type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error))
        else:
            print("PASS " + name)
    if failures:
        print("NEGATIVE TEST FAILURES=" + str(len(failures)))
        return 1
    print("ALL NEGATIVE TESTS PASS")
    return 0


def run_demo():
    root = new_run_folder() / "demo"
    machine = Machine(root)
    machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    machine.telemetry(
        device_id="CLASSROOM-1", state="ready",
        event="boot", elapsed_seconds=0
    )
    restarted = Machine(root)
    restart_result = "ALLOWED"
    try:
        restarted.authorize()
    except Denied:
        restart_result = "DENIED"
    print("DEMO active=" + restarted.state["active"] + " queued=" + str(len(restarted.state["queue"])))
    print("DEMO restart_policy=" + restart_result)
    print("BASELINE_SHA256=" + BASELINE_DIGEST)
    print("CANDIDATE_SHA256=" + CANDIDATE_DIGEST)
    print("DEMO evidence=classroom-fixtures-only; no inference or device measurement")
    return 0


def run_changed_task():
    root = new_run_folder()
    clock = {"mono": 0.0}
    mono = lambda: clock["mono"]
    policy_machine = Machine(root / "expired", monotonic=mono)
    policy_machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    clock["mono"] = 31.0
    expired_result = "ALLOWED"
    try:
        policy_machine.authorize()
    except Denied:
        expired_result = "DENIED"

    fallback_machine = Machine(root / "fallback")
    fallback_machine.reauthorize(AUTH_FIXTURE)
    fallback_machine.update()
    (fallback_machine.root / "candidate.bin").write_bytes(b"corrupt")
    restarted = Machine(fallback_machine.root)
    fallback_result = "NOT-CONTAINED"
    try:
        restarted.recover(False)
    except Denied:
        fallback_result = "CONTAINED"
    print("CHANGED expired_policy=" + expired_result)
    print("CHANGED incompatible_fallback=" + fallback_result)
    print("CHANGED external_effect_replayed=no")
    return 0


def run_probe(root):
    machine = Machine(Path(root))
    try:
        machine.authorize()
    except Denied as error:
        if (
            str(error) == "safe mode"
            and machine.state["safe"] is True
            and machine.state["reason"] == "restart-reauthorization-required"
        ):
            print(
                "PROBE restart_policy=DENIED "
                "reason=restart-reauthorization-required"
            )
            return 0
    print("PROBE restart_policy=INVALID reason=unexpected-state")
    return 1


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    modes = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    modes.add_argument("--demo", action="store_true")
    modes.add_argument("--tests", action="store_true")
    modes.add_argument("--changed-task", action="store_true")
    modes.add_argument("--probe-root")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.demo:
        return run_demo()
    if args.tests:
        return run_tests()
    if args.changed_task:
        return run_changed_task()
    return run_probe(args.probe_root)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

sections.title: Save, run, diagnose, and independently verify
paragraphs: From the folder containing `edge_operations.py`, run `python3.11 edge_operations.py --demo`. Exact expected stdout is five lines: `DEMO active=baseline queued=1`, `DEMO restart_policy=DENIED`, `BASELINE_SHA256=932d8e5a203d4c867e770d74ecb7c5e3e6d2d652a168143123b1579cb56534b2`, `CANDIDATE_SHA256=d7db9091598c61c4e09f96c4c9552b904f5d08bbffe7402ffc6510d77e468d66`, and `DEMO evidence=classroom-fixtures-only; no inference or device measurement`. The restart denial is intentional. The demonstration reconstructs the machine in one interpreter, while the negative suite separately launches the reviewed file in a new Python process and captures its stable probe output. Neither form may inherit the prior session-bound monotonic lease.

Run `python3.11 edge_operations.py --tests`. Exact successful stdout is: `PASS expiry, backward wall clock, and restart denial`; `PASS queue saturation, privacy, connectivity, and identity`; `PASS power loss at every persisted update boundary`; `PASS corrupted checkpoint and persisted artifact`; `PASS incompatible fallback and failed recovery`; `PASS nonfinite, negative, boolean, malformed, and over-limit readings`; and `ALL NEGATIVE TESTS PASS`. The successful process exit status is 0. Repeating the command creates a different learner-owned subfolder but prints the same lines.

A failed test prints `FAIL`, the test name, exception type, and diagnostic text. All remaining top-level tests still run. The final line becomes `NEGATIVE TEST FAILURES=N`, where N is the number of failed top-level tests, and the process exits with status 1. There is no unconditional green result. To inspect the exit status on a POSIX shell, run the tests and then run `echo $?`. Do not delete prior run folders to obtain a passing result. Inspect the newest folder under `edge_learning_runs`, its `manifest.json`, and its artifact files instead.

The drafting process has not executed these commands. Independent execution status is CANNOT VERIFY here. The required reviewer action is to save the exact file, run all three public modes with Python 3.11 or newer, compare stdout exactly, and confirm successful test status 0. The `--tests` mode itself starts the reviewed file in a subprocess for the restart probe. The reviewer must also deliberately alter one assertion to confirm aggregate failure status 1, restore the reviewed file, and repeat `--tests` to demonstrate independence from old state. The private `--probe-root` option exists for that subprocess test and is not a deployment-health interface.

sections.title: Changed task to solve before viewing the separate answer
paragraphs: Changed task: suppose a device has either of two conditions. Condition A is that its same-process policy lease has elapsed, including when its wall clock was moved backward. Condition B is that the candidate is active, its persisted bytes are corrupt, and the operator has no evidence that the baseline is a compatible fallback. Before running the answer, predict whether new work is authorized, whether recovery may claim a healthy baseline, and whether any uncertain external effect may be replayed.

Write down the causal sequence, not only the final state. For Condition A, identify which clock decides expiry and why a wall-clock correction does not renew authorization. For Condition B, identify which persisted bytes startup verifies, why the manifest cannot make corrupt bytes trustworthy, and why missing compatibility evidence blocks fallback. Then run the separate executable answer in the next section.

sections.title: Separate executable answer and causal feedback
paragraphs: Run `python3.11 edge_operations.py --changed-task`. Exact expected stdout is: `CHANGED expired_policy=DENIED`, `CHANGED incompatible_fallback=CONTAINED`, and `CHANGED external_effect_replayed=no`. Each invocation uses a new learner-owned run folder and retains older runs.

Separate answer: Condition A denies new work. The lease deadline was computed from the monotonic clock in the authorized process, so advancing monotonic time past 30 seconds expires the lease even if wall time moves backward. A process restart is stricter still: it invalidates the session-bound lease and requires explicit fixture reauthorization. Condition B remains contained with the candidate still recorded as active and corrupt. It does not silently label the baseline active because fallback compatibility was not established. No uncertain external effect is replayed because the classroom machine has no external-effect executor and requires the persisted uncertain-effects list to remain empty.

Causal feedback: authorization depends on trusted identity, a non-safe state, a session-matching policy, an in-memory monotonic deadline, and verified active bytes. Failure of any prerequisite denies before work. Recovery first checks the active artifact. If it is invalid, recovery may select the baseline only when compatibility is explicitly allowed and the baseline bytes independently match their immutable digest. Otherwise it persists `failed-recovery`, raises `Denied`, and remains contained. This prevents a recovery routine from manufacturing a healthy status.

sections.title: Actual conversion, inference, sustained qualification, and provider-neutral transfer
paragraphs: Actual converted-model inference requires evidence that the classroom program does not provide. Obtain the exact source revision and bytes from an authorized first-party distribution; record provenance and the applicable license decision; hash the source bytes; preserve the complete conversion or quantization command, configuration, calibration data identity, tool versions, and logs; hash the converted artifact; and record the application adapter, runtime, and execution provider. Load that converted artifact with the pinned target runtime and provider on the target device. Run representative, privacy-reviewed fixtures and compare the converted build with the approved reference over task-quality slices, safety boundaries, malformed inputs, numerical drift, latency distributions, memory pressure, storage growth, restart, and dependency failure. A file that converts successfully is not proof that its outputs, license, provider compatibility, or device performance are acceptable.

For sustained device energy and thermal qualification, identify the exact processor, accelerator, memory, storage, firmware, OS, secure-boot state, enclosure, cooling path, power source, runtime, provider, and artifact digest. Record calibrated instrument identities, calibration status, ambient conditions, fixture identity, sampling interval, warm-up method, load schedule, and test duration selected from the real duty cycle. Capture raw timestamps, input rate, output status, latency, memory, storage, utilization, temperature, instantaneous power, cumulative energy, throttling, errors, restarts, and shutdown events. Exercise mains or battery transitions, every supported connectivity state, prolonged disconnection, clock changes, reboot, staged update, rollback, and replacement. Preserve raw logs, analysis code, instrument exports, and operator observations. The temperature and watt inputs in `edge_operations.py` are only injected control-flow fixtures.

Acceptance requires a device and environment profile; source and converted artifact identities; license and provenance decision; reproducible conversion recipe; runtime and execution-provider compatibility; converted-build evaluation; sustained performance, power, energy, and thermal evidence; sensor calibration; offline, reconnect, identity, reboot, and clock evidence; telemetry and retention review; update-cohort records; rollback and replacement rehearsal; stop-condition evidence; fleet owner; and review date. Every missing item remains UNKNOWN or HOLD. Publication, classroom execution, or a model announcement is not deployment acceptance.

ONNX is a provider-neutral interchange format, while execution providers are runtime backends. ONNX Runtime documents its execution-provider architecture at https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/execution-providers/ (checked 2026-09-20). Transfer therefore depends on the exact exported artifact, operators used by that artifact, runtime and provider versions, target hardware, license, adapter, and measurements. It must not be inferred from a brand name.

Coverage for Meta, Qwen, Microsoft Phi, Mistral, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and NVIDIA is methodological only. For a candidate associated with any of these parties, obtain the candidate's dated first-party model documentation, revision, artifact identity, license terms, conversion guidance, and runtime or hardware evidence. Then execute the same conversion, quality, privacy, sustained-load, offline, update, and recovery qualification. This artifact makes no assumption that any named model has an ONNX export, a particular license, a supported execution provider, suitable edge capability, or acceptable performance. It offers no brand endorsement and no current-capability claim.

Model cards can record provenance, intended use, limitations, revision, and license metadata, as described by Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards (checked 2026-09-20). A model card is an input to qualification, not a replacement for artifact verification or target-device evidence. Data and telemetry boundaries must also be governed as AI risks, consistent with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework at https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework (checked 2026-09-20).

sections.title: ASSUMPTIONS
paragraphs: The original three runbook sections remain unchanged and these section identifiers will be appended to them.
The exact SHA-256 values supplied in the correction requirements correspond to the two literal fictional byte strings embedded in `edge_operations.py`.
A learner can run Python 3.11 or newer and create the relative learner-owned folder `edge_learning_runs` in the current working directory.
A UUID-named child folder satisfies the requirement that every invocation use a unique subfolder. The random folder name is deliberately not printed, so expected stdout remains deterministic.
The string `CLASSROOM-AUTH-FIXTURE` is a public test fixture, not a real credential or a production authentication design.

In-process reconstruction remains useful for deterministic unit coverage, but it is not treated as proof of an operating-system process restart. The negative suite additionally starts the same reviewed file through `sys.executable` over the same persisted folder, captures the child process result, and requires denial. Both reconstruction forms deliberately invalidate the session-bound lease and require explicit reauthorization.
